# Day One

> Day One helps an acquirer bring a newly acquired manufacturing plant’s purchasing under its spending rules before ERP migration. Kevin reads the plant’s records and coordinates buying. A NEAR testnet contract enforces authority and holds PO escrow through receipt and QC. The plant data is fictional and the committed demos replay recorded model outputs and testnet calls.

## Start with one order

[README.md](README.md) follows PO-1042 from a $5,150 refusal against a $2,500 limit to Linda’s approval, escrow funding, receipt and QC payment. The refused and funded calls carry the same signed model response. [PROOF.md](PROOF.md#the-purchasing-loop-po-1041-and-po-1042) lists the calls, signer accounts, gas payers, events and explorer links. The replay command is `npm run demo` after `npm ci` with Node 24.

The UI route `?judge=3` opens the refusal. `?judge=1` starts the handover walkthrough, and `?judge=summary` opens the other proofs. Run `npm run web:build`, then `npm run web` and use the address Vite prints, normally http://localhost:5173/. [Judge mode](docs/JUDGE_MODE.md) documents the route behavior.

## Reproduce the evidence

- `npm run prove` prints a scorecard whose rows and commands are defined in [scripts/lib/prove.ts](scripts/lib/prove.ts). It includes lint, typecheck and TypeScript tests. `-- --quick` skips that code check. `-- --contract` adds Rust unit and local sandbox tests.
- `npm run --silent prove -- --json` emits one JSON result with per-claim status, commands and failure causes. A failed testnet read produces a failed claim. `verify`, `verify:lot` and `verify:round` query testnet. Package installation also needs internet. The other replay checks use local fixtures.
- `npm run proof -- --check` checks that [PROOF.md](PROOF.md) matches the recordings. `npm run proof -- --live` re-queries the recorded transactions through archival RPC. The committed log contains 93 recorded transactions, including 23 deliberate contract refusals. These are separate from the 21 attack scenarios, several of which are stopped before a transaction.
- `npm run test:attacks` exercises those 21 recorded scenarios across Kevin, the mock ERP and the contract. Some succeed safely, such as the short delivery paying a reduced amount. [Attack evidence](data/proof-points.json).
- `npm run verify:attestation -- --offline` checks the stored report and 31 answer signatures using recorded hardware-verification verdicts. Without `--offline`, verification also contacts Intel and NVIDIA. [Recorded attestation](data/replay/attestation.json).
- [CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml) describes the automated checks. [README commands](README.md#try-it-no-keys-needed) provide individual replays, tamper verification and the Rust test entry point.

## Code and trust boundaries

| Component | Implementation and evidence | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Purchasing authority | [spend-policy](contracts/spend-policy/src/lib.rs), [approval tests](contracts/spend-policy/src/tests.rs), recorded refusal and approved retry in [PROOF.md](PROOF.md) | The contract compares approver, supplier, amount, category and the supplied fingerprint under the PO ID. Kevin supplies the fingerprint. Quantity is a separate input. |
| Signed decisions | [signer recovery](contracts/spend-policy/src/attest.rs), [decision and settlement tests](contracts/spend-policy/src/tests/settlement.rs) | HQ registers the signer following off-chain attestation verification. Plant B’s plain-PO policy requires a decision above $2,500. The contract checks a signed APPROVE for the supplied hash. Inputs remain trusted. |
| Quantity binding | `v2_trusts_the_agent_to_bind_quantity_to_the_approved_hash` in [settlement.rs](contracts/spend-policy/src/tests/settlement.rs) | This executable test demonstrates that v2 accepts a changed quantity with the same approved hash and signed decision, then settles against that changed quantity. It documents a limitation. |
| Receipt and payment | [settlement tests](contracts/spend-policy/src/tests/settlement.rs), [short-delivery transactions](PROOF.md#attacks-grounded-in-the-plant) | Count-based settlement requires an ordered quantity on a plain PO. A recorded invoice can cap payment. Pooled POs pay in full. Staff report the count and QC outcome. |
| Suppliers | [credentials](contracts/spend-policy/src/credentials.rs), [credential recordings](PROOF.md#supplier-credentials) | Credentials gate funding. QC payout keeps the agreed payee without rechecking credentials. HQ and supplier account keys remain trusted. |
| Plant operations | [Kevin](agents/kevin/src), [ledger](server/src/ledger) | Vision readings, planning, mailbox review, pricing and record citations are application behavior over fictional fixtures. A record anchor proves byte integrity. |
| Lot history | [lot book](server/src/lots), [root transactions](PROOF.md#lot-book-one-anchored-root-per-plant-per-day) | The seeded lot book contains 1,955 records under 416 daily roots, batch-anchored in nine calls. `npm run lots` checks it locally. `npm run verify:lot -- ASC-261116-01` also reads the root from testnet. |
| Acquirer’s books | [mock ERP](erp/src), [connector](server/src/erp-connector), `npm run erp:reconcile` | Seven checks compare the ledger, mock ERP and recorded chain views. ERP matching is outside the contract’s payment gate. |
| UI | [web](web/src), [export freshness check](scripts/web-data.ts) | Static replay plus seeded snapshots. Generated history and modeled money figures are labeled. The API supplies staff actions. |

## Other recorded flows

- `npm run demo:group` replays two plants pooling PO-G-2001, with each director approving their plant’s share. Lakeview stays out. [Group transactions](PROOF.md#group-purchase-po-g-2001).
- `npm run sealed` replays the commit-and-reveal round and its refused early, altered and late calls. Transaction arguments remain public, including refused reveals. [Round transactions](PROOF.md#sealed-quote-round-rfq-2611-02).
- `npm run usdc` replays PO-1047 paying 19.00 Circle testnet USDC. This uses the earlier contract code. [USDC transactions](PROOF.md#po-1047-in-circle-testnet-usdc).
- `npm run review`, `npm run ask`, `npm run brief` and `npm run books` expose local plant workflows. The mailbox is invented. Talk to Kevin has six recorded questions. [Command reference](README.md#try-it-no-keys-needed).

## Prototype scope

All transactions use testnet. The main run settles in DTUSD on `spend-policy-v2.acme-holdings.testnet`. Circle testnet USDC uses `spend-policy-usdc.acme-holdings.testnet` on earlier code. The old DTUSD account `spend-policy.acme-holdings.testnet` remains readable. The main run’s fictional dates are Nov 9–16, 2026. Other flows have their own recorded transactions.

SMS is simulated, staff keys are server-held, suppliers are rule-based and the ERP is a mock. Full-access keys remain under operator control. Packing-slip fields are fixture-driven. The model uses a shared signing key per model, and attestation establishes provenance. The PO escrow implements purchasing settlement. General multisig functionality is outside its scope. [Complete limitations](README.md#limitations).

Built by DadMod for NEAR HACKATHON. [README credits](README.md#built-with) disclose the human and AI contributions and the builder’s independent entry. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` describe the builders’ workflow. [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [contract specification](docs/CONTRACTS.md) and [lessons](docs/LESSONS.md) provide further context.
